server <- function(input, output, session) {

 observeEvent(input$file, {
   f <- read.csv(input$file$datapath)
   updateSelectInput(session, "columns", "Select Columns", choices = names(f))
 })

 dulieu <- eventReactive(input$choice, {
   req(input$file)
   inFile <- input$file
   read.csv(input$file$datapath)

 })

 output$table_display <- renderTable({
   f <- dulieu()

   bienpt <- subset(f, select = input$columns)
 })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

    #for cross validation

was doing, but you certainly shouldn't be a returning a function from a renderTable({}) call. You should return a tabular object (like bienpt, for example).

messages.subject_clean: Random number generation in ggplot and Shiny
messages.body_plain:
I had not (I though the code was supposed to take care of that - I just skimmed through it).

Here's the code with some changes (I changed C to consts because that's an R function, and it's best to avoid conflicts).

Here's the full code:

library(shiny)
library(FinCal)
library(dplyr)
library(triangle)
library(ggplot2)

SEED <- 2017
ITERATIONS <- 5000
MILLION <- 1000000

salesIter <- function(consts, threshold = -1) {
  y1 <-
    rtriangle(ITERATIONS,
      consts$SALES_TRIANG_MIN,
      consts$SALES_TRIANG_MAX,
      consts$SALES_TRIANG_MODE)
  demDecl <-
    rnorm(
      ITERATIONS,
      mean = consts$DEM_DECL_FACTOR_MEAN,
      sd = consts$DEM_DECL_FACTOR_SD
    )

  yr1Demand <- round(y1, consts$DIGITS)
  y2 <- round(yr1Demand * demDecl, consts$DIGITS)
  yr2Demand <- ifelse(y2 <= threshold, 0.0, y2)
  yr3Demand <- round(yr2Demand * demDecl, consts$DIGITS)
  yr4Demand <- round(yr3Demand * demDecl, consts$DIGITS)

  sales <-
    data.frame(yr1Demand,
      yr2Demand,
      yr3Demand,
      yr4Demand)
  names(sales) <- c("Y1Sales", "Y2Sales", "Y3Sales", "Y4Sales")

  return (sales)
}

revenueIter <- function(consts, sales) {
  revenue <-
    data.frame(
      round(sales$Y1Sales * consts$PRICE, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y2Sales * consts$PRICE, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y3Sales * consts$PRICE, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y4Sales * consts$PRICE, consts$DIGITS)
    )
  names(revenue) <-
    c("Y1Revenue", "Y2Revenue", "Y3Revenue", "Y4Revenue")

  return (revenue)
}

varCostIter <- function(consts, sales) {
  varCostRate <-
    rnorm(ITERATIONS,
      mean = consts$VAR_COST_RATE_MEAN,
      sd = consts$VAR_COST_RATE_SD)
  varCost <-
    data.frame(
      round(sales$Y1Sales * varCostRate, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y2Sales * varCostRate, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y3Sales * varCostRate, consts$DIGITS),
      round(sales$Y4Sales * varCostRate, consts$DIGITS)
    )
  names(varCost) <-
    c("Y1VarCost", "Y2VarCost", "Y3VarCost", "Y4VarCost")

  return (varCost)
}

fixedCostIter <- function(consts) {
  fixedCost <-
    runif(ITERATIONS,
      min = consts$FIX_COST_RATE_MIN,
      max = consts$FIX_COST_RATE_MAX)

  return (fixedCost)
}

cashFlow <- function(consts, revenue, varCost, fixedCost) {
  cashFlow <-
    data.frame(
      revenue$Y1Revenue - varCost$Y1VarCost - fixedCost,
      revenue$Y2Revenue - varCost$Y2VarCost - fixedCost,
      revenue$Y3Revenue - varCost$Y3VarCost - fixedCost,
      revenue$Y4Revenue - varCost$Y4VarCost - fixedCost
    )
  names(cashFlow) <- c("Y1", "Y2", "Y3", "Y4")

  return (cashFlow)
}

cashFlowNpv <- function(consts, cashFlow) {
  n <- NULL
  outlay <- -1 * consts$OUTLAY * MILLION
  j <- ITERATIONS
  for (i in c(1:j)) {
    j <- cashFlow[i:i, ]
    yearlyCashFlow <- c(outlay, j$Y1, j$Y2, j$Y3, j$Y4)
    n <-
      append(n, round(npv(
        r = consts$HURDLE_RATE, cf = yearlyCashFlow
      ), consts$DIGITS))
  }
  cashFlowNpv <- mutate(cashFlow, npvY0 = n)

  return (cashFlowNpv)
}

salesCashFlowNpv <- function(consts, sales, cfNpv) {
  salesCashFlowNpv <- data.frame(
    Y1Sales = sales$Y1Sales,
    Y1CashFlow = cfNpv$Y1,
    Y2Sales = sales$Y2Sales,
    Y2CashFlow = cfNpv$Y2,
    Y3Sales = sales$Y3Sales,
    Y3CashFlow = cfNpv$Y3,
    Y4Sales = sales$Y4Sales,
    Y4CashFlow = cfNpv$Y4,
    NPV = cfNpv$npvY0
  )

  return(salesCashFlowNpv)

}

npvCdf <- function(n) {
  N <- sort(n)
  P <- ecdf(N)
  return(P)
}

getBreakEven <- function(consts, n) {
  x <- filter(n, NPV >= 0)
  breakEvenNpv = min(x$NPV)
  breakEvenSales = round(select(filter(x, round(NPV, consts$DIGITS) == breakEvenNpv),
    Y1Sales)$Y1Sales, 0)

  return(breakEvenSales)
}

npdDistribution <- function(consts, m) {
  N <- m$NPV / MILLION

  P <- npvCdf(N)
  #
  # NPV distribution curve
  n <- sort(N)
  p <- P(n) * 100
  df <- data.frame(npv = n, odds = p)

  return(df)
}

pointsOnPlot <- function(consts, m) {
  # Points of interest
  s <- getBreakEven(consts, m)
  o <- consts$NPV_BREAK_EVEN_WORST_ODDS

  w <- o * 100

  n <- m$NPV / MILLION
  n <- sort(n)
  q <- round((quantile(n, o)), consts$DIGITS)
  e <- consts$NPV_BREAK_EVEN_VALUE
  b <- npvCdf(m$NPV / MILLION)(0) * 100

  p <- data.frame(s, o, w, q, e, b)
  names(p) <- c("s", "o", "w", "q", "e", "b")

  return(p)
}

makePlot <- function(d, p) {
  # Labels
  npvOdds <- paste("Odds of break-even : ", p$b, "%")
  salesThresh <- paste("Sales threshold : ", p$s)
  worstCase <-
    paste("Worst case (@ 5% odds) : ", p$q, "million")

  #
  # Make plot
  #

  g <- ggplot(d, aes(x = d$npv, y = d$odds)) +

    geom_line(colour = "blue") +

    labs(title = "Net Present Value (NPV) and Odds") +

    labs(x = "NPV (million)") +
    labs(y = "Percent (%)") +

    geom_vline(xintercept = p$e,

      colour = "red",
      linetype = "longdash") +

    geom_hline(yintercept = p$b,

      colour = "green",
      linetype = "longdash") +

    geom_vline(xintercept = p$q,

      colour = "green",
      linetype = "dotdash") +

    geom_hline(yintercept = p$w,
      colour = "red",
      linetype = "dotdash") +
    annotate("text", x=4, y=75, label=npvOdds)
  return (g)
}

buildOutputTable <- function(consts, p) {
  outputTable <-
    data.frame(consts$OUTLAY, consts$HURDLE_RATE * 100, p$b, p$s, p$q)
  names(outputTable) <-
    c("Outlay (mn)",
      "Hurdle Rate (%)",
      "BE Odds (%)",
      "BE Sales",
      "Wconsts Loss (mn)")

  return(outputTable)
}

npvCalc <- function(consts, threshold = -1) {
  s <- salesIter(consts, threshold)
  r <- revenueIter(consts, s)
  v <- varCostIter(consts, s)
  f <- fixedCostIter(consts)
  c <- cashFlow(consts, r, v, f)
  n <- cashFlowNpv(consts, c)
  t <- salesCashFlowNpv(consts, s, n)

  return (t)
}

npvPlot <- function(consts, threshold = -1) {
  set.seed(consts$SEED)
  n <- npvCalc(consts, threshold)
  d <- npdDistribution(consts, n)
  p <- pointsOnPlot(consts, n)
  g <- makePlot(d, p)

  return(g)
}

npvTable <- function(consts, threshold=-1) {
  set.seed(consts$SEED)
  n <- npvCalc(consts, threshold)
  d <- npdDistribution(consts, n)
  p <- pointsOnPlot(consts, n)
  t <- buildOutputTable(consts, p)

  return(t)
}

getConstants <- function(input) {
  consts <- data.frame(
    SEED,
    3,
    100,
    0.0,
    0.05,
    input$outlay,
    input$hurdleRate,

    input$salesRange[1],
    input$salesRange[2],
    input$salesMode,
    input$demDeclMean,
    input$demDeclSd,
    input$varCostMean,
    input$varCostSd,
    input$fixedCostRange[1],
    input$fixedCostRange[2]
  )

  names(consts) <-
    c("SEED",
      "DIGITS",
      "PRICE",
      "NPV_BREAK_EVEN_VALUE",
      "NPV_BREAK_EVEN_WORST_ODDS",
      "OUTLAY",

      "HURDLE_RATE",
      "SALES_TRIANG_MIN",
      "SALES_TRIANG_MAX",

      sliderInput("fixedCostRange",
        label = "Fixed Costs - Min and Max",
        min = 30000, max = 50000, value = c(36000, 44000)),
      sliderInput("varCostMean",
        label = "Variable Costs - Mean",
        min = 10, max = 50, value = 20),
      sliderInput("varCostSd",
        label = "Variable Costs - SD",
        min = 1, max = 10, value = 3)
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("npdPlot"),
      tableOutput("npdTable")
    )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  output$npdPlot <- renderPlot({
    print(reactiveValuesToList(input))
    npvOddsPlot(reactiveValuesToList(input))

    npvOddsTable(input)
  })
}

messages.subject_clean: "Error using package" when adding "runtime: shiny" to yml-header in RMarkdown
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

the following code works totally fine as a simple RMarkdown but gives the error "Error using package 1. Object bPols not found" if I add "runtime: shiny". I think it is because the library "maptools" is not loaded correctly if I use "runtime: shiny" but why? And how can I solve it?

Kind regards

---
title: "Untitled"
author: "Jennifer R. Marlon et al."
date: "3 Mai 2017"
output: html_document
runtime: shiny
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

This is the code used to produce the results and figures seen in "A space-time statistical
climate model for hurricane intensification in the North Atlantic basin" by Fraza, Elsner and Jagger.

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library("dplyr")
load("mjoBestUse.RData")

Tracks.df = filter(Tracks.df, Int >= 33.0)
```

```{r}

fullData.df = load("best.use.2014.Rdata")
begin = 1975; end = 2014

fullData.df = best.use %>%
  mutate(Int = WmaxS * .5144,
         DIntDt = DWmaxDt * .5144) %>%
  filter(Yr >= begin, Yr <= end, Int >= 33.0, M == FALSE)

```

```{r}
library("rgdal")
ll = "+proj=longlat +ellps=WGS84"

Tracks.sdf = Tracks.df
coordinates(Tracks.sdf) = c("lon", "lat")
proj4string(Tracks.sdf) = CRS(ll)

fullData.sdf = fullData.df
coordinates(fullData.sdf) = c("lon", "lat")
proj4string(fullData.sdf) = CRS(ll)
```

Create grid
```{r}
library("raster")
r = raster(ncol = 10, nrow = 5,
           xmn = -100, xmx = -20,
           ymn = 10, ymx = 50)

Tracks.grid = rasterize(Tracks.sdf, r,
                        field = 'DIntDt',
                        fun = mean)

test = rasterToPolygons(Tracks.grid)

Example.sdf = subset(Tracks.sdf,
                     Sid == 1675 |
```

messages.subject: Re: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.subject_clean: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.body_plain:
This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.

The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())

you should be calling it like this:

callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.

Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".

Then,

  observeEvent(input$fileName,{
  #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
  dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
  })

should all be replaced by

dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)

and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.

You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html

I hope that helps!

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Thanks a lot for the explanations. It helped a lot. Now I am facing my next anticipated issue as I have several modules.

Once the data is clustered, I would like my other modules to be updated. I have some density plot and scatter plot modules, which can color per factor, so I would like the list of variables, and the data to be updated for them as well. So they should react to clustering process.

The solution I have found based on your help, is to pass 2 arguments to other modules.

 callModule(kdash_density,"DensPlots",dataInput,dataClustered)

 dataClustered<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)

So my density plot module gets an updated list if dataClustered is not NULL. This works, but that requires to put some logic in the plot modules, and as many arguments as the nuber of modules susceptible to modify data (PCA module, standardization module, ...).

I tried in my server to do :
 observeEvent(input$Refresh,{
      dataInput<-dataClustered
      output$Debug<-renderPrint(head(dataInput()))
    })
That works, and displays my updated table, so I guess i can update dataInput.

However modules such as:

callModule(kdash_scatter,"Scatter",dataInput) keep the old list of variables from original dataInput, without added variable from clustering module.

I guess I do not use updateSelectInput correctly within the module:

#Scatter plot module
kdash_scatter <- function(input, output, session, data) {

  observeEvent(data(),{
    updateSelectInput(session, "XAxis", choices = names(data()))
    updateSelectInput(session, "YAxis", choices = names(data()))
    updateSelectInput(session, "ZAxis", choices = names(data()))
    updateSelectInput(session, "ColorAxis", choices = names(data()))
  })
 }

I guess I am still missing a point on reactivity.

Basically what I did not manage to make work, is to replace dataInput by dataCluster, without the need to add an extra argument to my modules.

As I will implement several modules which will add to data or transform data, I would prefer to be able to overwrite dataInput, and make all modules react to that, rather than adding arguments for each possible transformation.

Thanks for your help.

On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 1:44 AM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.
>
> The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:
>
> callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
>
> you should be calling it like this:
>
> callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)
>
> The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.
>
> Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".
>
> Then,
>
>   observeEvent(input$fileName,{
>   #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
>   dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
>   })
>
> should all be replaced by
>
> dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)
>
> and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.
>
> You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html
>
> I hope that helps!
>
> On Tue, May 2, 2017 at 3:15 AM Kamal Hami-Eddine <kham...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Hi,
> >
> > I am writing my first Shiny app, and my goal is to simply wrap some basic R functions to analyze and plot some data.
> > I would like to use modules to organize my code, but I have a problem right now, as I can not get updated data frame out of my module.
> >
> > I read an ascii file (attached to the message) in my server. I would like then to perform clustering on this data in a separate module.
> > After te clustering is done, I would like to add a class column to my data frame, by pressing a button. Things seems to be ok within my clustering module, as my data summary shows the column with the right name.
> > However, it seems I can not return this data frame to my server, to then use in plots.
> >
> > At the end of the day, I would like some modules to update my dataInput reactive data frame, and others to be updated accordingly (happends at the end of my server code below).
> >
> > I spent quite some time on that without finding the solution, and being new to Shiny and reactive programming, I feel I reached my limits trying to find out alone.
> >
> > My example below runs locally, I hope it illustrates my issue ok.
> >
> > Thanks.
> >
> > App UI code:
> > ## app.R ##
> >
> >
> > options(autoWidth = TRUE)
> >
> > header<- dashboardHeader(title = "Question?")
> >
> > #Define content of sidebar
> > sidebar<- dashboardSidebar(

> >   )
> > )

> > #Dasboard body definition. Gives content of each dashboard entry

> >       # Boxes need to be put in a row (or column)

> >       fluidRow(
> >         infoBoxOutput("info_var"),

> >       fluidRow(

> >       fluidRow(box(title="Refresh Data"),  actionButton(inputId="Refresh", label="Refresh data")),
> >       fluidRow(
> >         box(title="Data frame", status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE,
> >             collapsible = TRUE,
> >             tableOutput('contents'),width="100%")
> >       )
> >     ),
> >     tabItem(tabName="clustering",
> >             h2="Descriptive statistics on input data",
> >             kdash_clustering_UI("ClustUI")
> >     )
> >   )
> > )
> >
> > #Run UI
> > ui <- dashboardPage(header,sidebar,body,skin="black")
> >
> >
> >
> > Server Code:
> > options(shiny.maxRequestSize=100*1024^2)
> > options(autoWidth = TRUE)
> > source("./KDash_rainbow_palette.R")
> > source("./KDash_legend.R")
> >
> > server <- function(input, output,session) {
> >
> >   #load text file
> >   dataInput <- reactive({
> >     # input$file1 will be NULL initially. After the user selects

> >

> >

> >     if(input$filetype==" "){

> >       if(input$standardize_data==TRUE){

> >     }else{

> >       }
> >     }
> >
> >
> >     dataIn
> >   })
> >
> >   #render content of Info box for variable number and line number
> >   output$info_var <- renderInfoBox({
> >     infoBox(
> >       "Nb variables", ncol(dataInput()), icon = icon("list"),
> >       color = "navy"
> >     )
> >   })
> >   output$info_lines <- renderInfoBox({
> >     infoBox(
> >       "Nb lines", nrow(dataInput()), icon = icon("list"),
> >       color = "olive"
> >     )
> >   })
> >
> >   #Render content of combo box containing variable names
> >
> >
> >   output$contents <- renderTable({
> >     dataInput()
> >   })
> >
> >   observeEvent(input$fileName,{
> >   #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
> >   dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
> >   })
> >
> >   observeEvent(input$Refresh,{
> >   output$Debug<-renderPrint(head(dataInput()))
> >   })
> > }
> >
> >
> > Clustering Module:
> >
> > kdash_clustering_UI<- function(id) {
> >   ns <- NS(id)
> >   fluidPage(
> >     fluidRow(
> >       box(title="Matrix plot of clustered data",
> >           plotOutput(ns("MatrixClust")),status = "primary", solidHeader = TRUE,
> >           collapsible = TRUE
> >       ),
> >       box(title="Clustering Controls",
> >           selectInput(ns("ClustMethod"),"Select clustering method",choices=c("Hierarchical-Ward","Hierarchical-Single",
> >                                                                              "Hierarchical-Complete","Hierarchical-Average(UPGMA)",
> >                                                                              "Hierarchical-McQuitty(WPGMA)","Hierarchical-Median(WPGMC)",
> >                                                                              "Hierarchical-Centroid(UPGMC)","KMeans"),multiple=F),
> >           sliderInput(ns("NbClust"),"Select Number of Classes",min=1,max=100,value=10),
> >           selectInput(ns("ClustVariables"),"Select variables to use for clustering","",multiple=T),
> >           actionButton(inputId=ns("SaveClusters"), label="Save Clusters"),

messages.subject: hosting HTML pages on shiny-server
messages.subject_clean: hosting HTML pages on shiny-server
messages.body_plain:
I have used a combination of shiny and rmarkdown to build a website, in which the shiny app makes the search feature filtering results from a large database. Every result is linked by name to a detailed page where more information is provided. In practice, the app returns a result table in which each row of the name column is a link to the specific info page.

It seems however that shiny-server (installed on our server) does not allow hosting of html pages, so the link to the info page is broken -Not Found .

Alternatively, I am trying to render the info-page as a general rmarkdown page that is rendered with result-specific information every time it is called. Unfortunately, there does not seem to be a way to pass down information through a link to a general rmarkdown document. In practice, what I want to implement: clicking on the result 'My result', a generic .rmd document is called and the same link passes down the name 'My result' to the .rmd so that it can retrieve 'My result'- specific information before being knitted.

Is there a solution to this using shiny-server?

Thanks,

Edith

messages.subject: Re: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.subject_clean: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.body_plain:
You definitely do NOT want to do this: "dataInput <- dataClustered" And this isn't doing what you think it is anyway, it's just creating a new local variable dataInput and assigning it the value dataClustered; this is not replacing the original dataInput in any way.

What is the relationship between kdash_clustering and kdash_density? kdash_density needs to see the changes that kdash_clustering makes, is the converse true as well (does kdash_clustering need to see the changes that kdash_density makes)?

If you have not done it yet, I highly suggest you watch Effective Reactive Programming parts 1 & 2 on this page: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/

>
>  callModule(kdash_density,"DensPlots",dataInput,dataClustered)
>
>  dataClustered<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)
>

> > This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.
> >
> > The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:
> >
> > callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
> >
> > you should be calling it like this:
> >
> > callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)
> >
> > The way to think of the original code is, "pass a snapshot of the current value of dataInput to kdash_clustering", while the corrected code is, "make all (current and future) values of dataInput available to kdash_clustering". And the latter is what you want.
> >
> > Similarly, when returning data_clustered from inside kdash_clustering, you're saying "return(data_clustered())" when it should be "return(data_clustered)". Again, the former means "return a snapshot of the current value of data_clustered" when you really mean "make all (current and future) values of data_clustered available to whomever is calling me".
> >
> > Then,
> >
> >   observeEvent(input$fileName,{
> >   #dataOutput<- eventReactive(dataInput(),{
> >   dataInput()<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput())
> >   })
> >
> > should all be replaced by
> >
> > dataClustered <- callModule(kdash_clustering, "ClustUI", dataInput)
> >
> > and dataClustered() should be used in any reactive expressions or outputs or observers that want to access the post-clustered data.
> >
> > You should also look into using req to deal with NULL values of input$fileName. https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html
> >
> > I hope that helps!
> >
> > On Tue, May 2, 2017 at 3:15 AM Kamal Hami-Eddine <kham...@gmail.com> wrote:

kdash_clustering is running calculation and modifies the data frame, while kdash_density is just a plotting module. So kdash_density needs to be udated, but the opposite is not necessary.

messages.subject: Re: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.subject_clean: Use modules to update a data frame, and send back updated result to server.
messages.body_plain:
The first question I think you have to answer is whether the calculation modules *modify* the data frame, or *transform* it. The former implies that the original value is changed in-place, while the latter implies that a new copy is created by the module and downstream modules look at the new copy.

For example, say you have a module that does some smoothing on the data. If you take the former approach, you might have UI that consists of some smoothing parameters and a "Smooth" button; clicking the Smooth button modifies the original data. The advantage(?) is that you can perform this smooth multiple times, and in any order of operations relative to any other task being performed (like you can do it before or after you do some subsetting with a different module). The disadvantage is you can't undo the smoothing operation (at least not without a bunch more work).

If you take the latter approach, the UI might be just the smoothing parameters, no "Smooth" button to push (unless it is a very slow operation), and you can see what it looks like with different parameter values just by moving sliders around. The disadvantage is that you, the app author, need to decide when this smoothing should be performed relative to other modules like subsetting; the app user is not able to make their own decision about it (without doing a bunch more work).

For this app, I would prefer the former approach with consists in modifying the data. I need to test different sequences, in possibly different orders. I will log the operations in a report, so I keep track of the changes I apply, so undo won't be necessary for this first stage.
Thanks a lot for your help.

On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 10:49 PM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> The first question I think you have to answer is whether the calculation modules *modify* the data frame, or *transform* it. The former implies that the original value is changed in-place, while the latter implies that a new copy is created by the module and downstream modules look at the new copy.
>
> For example, say you have a module that does some smoothing on the data. If you take the former approach, you might have UI that consists of some smoothing parameters and a "Smooth" button; clicking the Smooth button modifies the original data. The advantage(?) is that you can perform this smooth multiple times, and in any order of operations relative to any other task being performed (like you can do it before or after you do some subsetting with a different module). The disadvantage is you can't undo the smoothing operation (at least not without a bunch more work).
>
> If you take the latter approach, the UI might be just the smoothing parameters, no "Smooth" button to push (unless it is a very slow operation), and you can see what it looks like with different parameter values just by moving sliders around. The disadvantage is that you, the app author, need to decide when this smoothing should be performed relative to other modules like subsetting; the app user is not able to make their own decision about it (without doing a bunch more work).
>
> On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 9:41 AM Kamal Hami-Eddine <kham...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Thank you for the link.
> >
> > kdash_clustering is running calculation and modifies the data frame, while kdash_density is just a plotting module. So kdash_density needs to be udated, but the opposite is not necessary.
> >
> > I was planning to build the app by separating calculation modules, which will update the data frame, from plotting and qc modules which will just read the data and display it (thus need to be updated from data updates by calculation modules).
> >
> > I will look at the videos first and try to make my way through.
> >
> > Thank you.
> >
> > On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 6:27 PM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > You definitely do NOT want to do this: "dataInput <- dataClustered" And this isn't doing what you think it is anyway, it's just creating a new local variable dataInput and assigning it the value dataClustered; this is not replacing the original dataInput in any way.
> > >
> > > What is the relationship between kdash_clustering and kdash_density? kdash_density needs to see the changes that kdash_clustering makes, is the converse true as well (does kdash_clustering need to see the changes that kdash_density makes)?
> > >
> > > If you have not done it yet, I highly suggest you watch Effective Reactive Programming parts 1 & 2 on this page: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/
> > >
> > > On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 1:44 AM Kamal Hami-Eddine <kham...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > > Hi Joe,
> > > >
> > > > Thanks a lot for the explanations. It helped a lot. Now I am facing my next anticipated issue as I have several modules.
> > > >
> > > > Once the data is clustered, I would like my other modules to be updated. I have some density plot and scatter plot modules, which can color per factor, so I would like the list of variables, and the data to be updated for them as well. So they should react to clustering process.
> > > >
> > > > The solution I have found based on your help, is to pass 2 arguments to other modules.
> > > >
> > > >  callModule(kdash_density,"DensPlots",dataInput,dataClustered)
> > > >
> > > >  dataClustered<-callModule(kdash_clustering,"ClustUI",dataInput)
> > > >
> > > > So my density plot module gets an updated list if dataClustered is not NULL. This works, but that requires to put some logic in the plot modules, and as many arguments as the nuber of modules susceptible to modify data (PCA module, standardization module, ...).
> > > >
> > > > I tried in my server to do :
> > > >  observeEvent(input$Refresh,{
> > > >       dataInput<-dataClustered
> > > >       output$Debug<-renderPrint(head(dataInput()))
> > > >     })
> > > > That works, and displays my updated table, so I guess i can update dataInput.
> > > >
> > > > However modules such as:
> > > >
> > > > callModule(kdash_scatter,"Scatter",dataInput) keep the old list of variables from original dataInput, without added variable from clustering module.
> > > >
> > > > I guess I do not use updateSelectInput correctly within the module:
> > > >
> > > > #Scatter plot module
> > > > kdash_scatter <- function(input, output, session, data) {
> > > >
> > > >   observeEvent(data(),{
> > > >     updateSelectInput(session, "XAxis", choices = names(data()))
> > > >     updateSelectInput(session, "YAxis", choices = names(data()))
> > > >     updateSelectInput(session, "ZAxis", choices = names(data()))
> > > >     updateSelectInput(session, "ColorAxis", choices = names(data()))
> > > >   })
> > > >  }
> > > >
> > > > I guess I am still missing a point on reactivity.
> > > >
> > > > Basically what I did not manage to make work, is to replace dataInput by dataCluster, without the need to add an extra argument to my modules.
> > > >
> > > > As I will implement several modules which will add to data or transform data, I would prefer to be able to overwrite dataInput, and make all modules react to that, rather than adding arguments for each possible transformation.
> > > >
> > > > Thanks for your help.
> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 1:44 AM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > > > > This topic has not been fleshed out enough in the documentation, sorry. You have the right idea, but some important fixes need to be made.
> > > > >
> > > > > The `data` input parameter to your module server function, should not be a data frame; rather, it should be a reactive expression that yields a data frame. So instead of calling it like this from server.R:

messages.subject: Loading animations for Shiny outputs (shinycssloaders)
messages.subject_clean: Loading animations for Shiny outputs (shinycssloaders)
messages.body_plain:
Hi Shiny Users,

It seems to have been a common request to have loading animations for Shiny outputs (e.g. plots, tables), to show the user some progress whilst calculations are running (without having to create a global progress-bar).

Leveraging on Shiny JS events and the loading animations at https://projects.lukehaas.me/css-loaders/, I have created a mini-package called shinycssloaders <https://github.com/andrewsali/shinycssloaders> that solves this tasks with requiring very minimal additional code from the Shiny developer (just wrap your output function call using the withSpinner function in the package). The animations automatically show / hide when the calculations are running / done or if the output is not generated (e.g. a req() or validate() cancels the output).

An example Shiny app to test is given at https://frontside.shinyapps.io/example/

For further information, please refer to the github page <https://github.com/andrewsali/shinycssloaders>.

I hope some people will find this useful!

Cheers,

Andras

  alphacen<-numericInput("alphacen",label=h5(strong("Alpha CENER")),

  clit<-numericInput("clit",label=h5(strong("Temperatura de la celula del cliente")),
                         value=25,step=0.25,width='80%')
  sep<-radioButtons(inputId='sep',label='Separadores',
                    choices=c(Coma=',',PuntoComa=';',Tabulacion='\t',Espacio=''),

  vertodo<-checkboxInput(inputId='vertodo',label="Aumentar las graficas",FALSE)

    file1<-input$file1
  if(is.null(file1)){return()}
  df<-read.csv(file=file1$datapath,sep=input$sep,skip=50,
                col.names=colnames,fileEncoding="UCS-2LE")
  })

  datosvalidos<-function(){
    df<-data()

    ## Damos formato a la variable Tiempo
    df$Tiempo<-strptime(df$Tiempo, format="%d/%m/%Y%H:%M:%S")
    df$Tiempo<-as.POSIXct(df$Tiempo)

    ## Ordenamos el dataframe segun la fecha
    df<-arrange(df,Tiempo)

    ## Extraemos los dias de los que se estan tratando los datos
    df<-mutate(df,dia=as.Date(df$Tiempo))
    dias<-unique(df$dia)

    ## Recorremos cada dia y extraemos sus datos validos
    df2Total<-NULL
    i<-1
    while(i<=length(dias)){
      dfi<-filter(df,dia==dias[i])

      ## Calculamos la elevacion solar para cada punto medido:
      dia<-as.POSIXlt(as.Date(dfi$Tiempo))$yday
      angdia<-(2*pi*(dia-1))/365
      decl<-0.006918-0.399912*cos(angdia)+
        0.070257*sin(angdia)-0.006758*cos(2*angdia)+
        0.000907*sin(2*angdia)-0.002697*cos(3*angdia)+
        0.00148*sin(3*angdia)

      mediodia<-paste(as.Date(dfi$Tiempo),"12:00:00")
      mediodia<-as.POSIXct(mediodia,format="%Y-%m-%d%H:%M:%S")
      mediodia<-mediodia[1]
      anghor<-as.numeric((2*pi*((dfi$Tiempo)-mediodia))/(24),units="hours")
      ## Coordenadas Sarriguren: 42.8N, 1.6W
      latitud<-2*pi*42.8/360
      angelev<-asin((sin(decl)*sin(latitud))+(cos(decl)*cos(latitud)*cos(anghor)))

      ## Anadimos el valor de AM para cada punto medido
      dfi<-mutate(dfi,AM=as.numeric((dfi$BAR)/(1013*sin(angelev))))
      rm(angdia,angelev,anghor,decl,latitud)

      ## Calculamos los valores maximos y minimos de irradiancias y corrientes
      ## En un periodo de 3 minutos
      vent<-12*3
      MaxDir<-rollapply(dfi$Directa1,width=vent,FUN=max,align="right",fill=1000)
      MinDir<-rollapply(dfi$Directa1,width=vent,FUN=min,align="right",fill=10)
      MaxDif<-rollapply(dfi$Difusa,width=vent,FUN=max,align="right",fill=1000)
      MinDif<-rollapply(dfi$Difusa,width=vent,FUN=min,align="right",fill=10)
      MaxIsc<-rollapply(dfi$Cli_V1,width=vent,FUN=max,align="right",fill=1000)
      MinIsc<-rollapply(dfi$Cli_V1,width=vent,FUN=min,align="right",fill=10)

      ## Anadimos al dataframe las variaciones en esos 3 minutos
      dfi<-mutate(dfi,VarDir=100*abs((MaxDir-MinDir)/MinDir),
                  VarDif=100*abs((MaxDif-MinDif)/MinDif),
                  VarIsc=100*abs((MaxIsc-MinIsc)/MinIsc),

      rm(vent,MaxDir,MinDir,MaxDif,MinDif,MaxIsc,MinIsc)

      df2<-filter(dfi,(dfi$Gt>800)&(dfi$Gt<1200)&(dfi$VarDir<3)&(dfi$VarDif<3)&
                    (dfi$VarIsc<3)&(dfi$Difusa/dfi$Gt>0.1)&
                    (dfi$Difusa/dfi$Gt<0.3)&(dfi$AM<3))

> On Thu, May 4, 2017 at 10:49 PM Joe Cheng <j...@rstudio.com> wrote:
> > The first question I think you have to answer is whether the calculation modules *modify* the data frame, or *transform* it. The former implies that the original value is changed in-place, while the latter implies that a new copy is created by the module and downstream modules look at the new copy.
> >
> > For example, say you have a module that does some smoothing on the data. If you take the former approach, you might have UI that consists of some smoothing parameters and a "Smooth" button; clicking the Smooth button modifies the original data. The advantage(?) is that you can perform this smooth multiple times, and in any order of operations relative to any other task being performed (like you can do it before or after you do some subsetting with a different module). The disadvantage is you can't undo the smoothing operation (at least not without a bunch more work).
> >
> > If you take the latter approach, the UI might be just the smoothing parameters, no "Smooth" button to push (unless it is a very slow operation), and you can see what it looks like with different parameter values just by moving sliders around. The disadvantage is that you, the app author, need to decide when this smoothing should be performed relative to other modules like subsetting; the app user is not able to make their own decision about it (without doing a bunch more work).

messages.body_plain:
Hi!

I am building a web site in WordPress and I want to create an iframe calling a Shiny.

I saw some tutorials on Internet about how to install shiny server in Amazon web services. But all of them have instructions using Linux. I have never used it and my computer is Windows.

Have I to use a Linux computer or just the Amazon server is in Linux and is possible to do it in Windows? Do I need a specific tutorial?

Sorry about the silly question and thanks in advance.

Regards,

Luis

messages.body_plain:
Luis,

You'll need Linux.  I'd use the latest Ubuntu 16.04.  There will be an image for it in the list of commonly used images ("Amazon Machine Images") when you launch your EC2 instance.

Here are some tips to get you started.

1. Install R:

sudo apt install r-base

2. Install shiny server using directions here:

https://www.rstudio.com/products/shiny/download-server/

3.  Set up your security zone to allow port 3838 to have open access to the internet in AWS.

4.  Upload your apps and test them

5.  If you need a domain name, I'd install nginx, listen on the domain name, and proxy_pass the requests to shiny.

6.  For an iframe to work, you also may need to do some stuff with CORS, it depends.

It's not impossible and if you plan on working with Linux in the future this would be a reasonable project to gain familiarity with the environment, the package manger (apt for ubuntu), and basic networking with AWS/Linux.

Erik

messages.subject: scoping issue: Shiny object found before object of same name in Global Env
messages.subject_clean: scoping issue: Shiny object found before object of same name in Global Env
messages.body_plain:
I have an Addin that creates and runs code based on user input.  The code is created as a string and then evaluated with eval-parse.

The relevant code is as follows:

command <- rv$code  # rv is a list of reactive values, rv$code is the code to run
eval(parse(text = command))

Suppose that a data framed named "a" is in the user's Global Environment when the Addin is called, and  user input results in rv$code having the value "xtabs(~ group, data = a)".  Then we would expect a table of the values of the variable "group" in the data frame "a".  Instead we get an error:  "'data' argument is of the wrong type."

I did some checking.  If you modify the relevant code as follows:

command <- rv$code
print(command)
print(a)
print(search())
eval(parse(text = command))

You discover that:

* The command-text is as expected.
* What's printed as "a" is the Shiny function tag$a, not the data frame a.
* Nevertheless, the Global Environment appears first on the search path, before the Shiny namespace.

Why, in the call to eval(), does R find the anchor-tag function instead of the data frame?

Thanks for any insight you can provide.

messages.subject: Re: Cannot render datatable
messages.subject_clean: Cannot render datatable
messages.body_plain:
You need to do:

  output$mytable1 <- DT::renderDataTable(

   breast, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 10)
 )

Instead of:

  output$mytable1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
   DT::datatable(breast, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 10))
 })

Also you have lots of repeated inputId s/ outputId s. You should fix that to.

Here's a working example, though I'd recommend you check out modules <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/modules.html> to avoid having to remember which ids are already taken:

library(shiny)
library(shinythemes)
library(DT)

cmc <- cars
breast <- faithful
haberman <- pressure

classifier <- tabPanel("Classifier",
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("algochoice1",
        "Select an Algorithm",
        choices = c(

          "K Nearest Neighbour (kNN)",
          "Decision Tree",
          "Naive Bayes",
          "Support Vector Machine (SVM)",
          "Artificial Neural Networks",
          "Fuzzy")
      ),

      selectInput("datachoice1",
        "Select a dataset",
        choices = c("Haberman", "CMC", "Breast Cancer")
      ),
      sliderInput("slider1",

        "Select Training:Test Dataset ratio",
        1, 99, value = 70, step = 10
      ),

      actionButton("action21", "Show",
        class = "btn-primary", style = ":right"
      )
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("coolplot1"),
      br(),
      br(),
      tableOutput("results1")
    )
  )
)

comparator <- tabPanel("Comparator",
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("datachoice2",
        "Select a dataset",
        choices = c("Haberman", "CMC", "Breast Cancer")
      ),
      sliderInput("slider2",

        "Select Training:Test Dataset ratio",
        1, 99, value = 70, step = 10
      ),

      radioButtons("typeInput2", "Graph Parameter",

        choices = c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Time"),
        selected = "Accuracy"
      ),

      actionButton("action22", "Show",
        class = "btn-primary", style = ":right"
      )
    ),
    mainPanel(
      plotOutput("coolplot2"),
      br(),
      br(),
      tableOutput("results2")
    )
  )
)

dataset <- tabPanel("Dataset",
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      selectInput("datachoice3", "Select a dataset",
        choices = c("Haberman", "CMC", "Breast Cancer")
      )
    ),
    mainPanel(
      DT::dataTableOutput('mytable0'),

      tabsetPanel(id = 'dataset1',
        tabPanel("Breast Cancer", DT::dataTableOutput('mytable1')),

        tabPanel("CMC", DT::dataTableOutput('mytable2')),

        tabPanel('Haberman', DT::dataTableOutput('mytable3'))
      )
    )
  )
)

ui <- fluidPage(theme = shinytheme("flatly"),

  titlePanel("Medical Data Classifier"),
  navbarPage("Navigation",

    classifier,
    comparator,
    dataset
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  # output$mytable0 <- DT::renderDataTable(
  #   breast, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 10)
  # )
  output$mytable1 <- DT::renderDataTable(

    breast, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 10)

  )
  output$mytable2 <- DT::renderDataTable(

    cmc, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 5)

  )
  output$mytable3 <- DT::renderDataTable(

    haberman, options = list(lengthMenu = c(5, 30, 50), pageLength = 10)
  )
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Hi Pedro,

You are possibly hitting rate limits imposed by Yahoo per IP address. If others are running similar API calls, you may or may not receive data, resulting in a bit of confusion as to why it works sometimes but not at other times.

https://developer.yahoo.com/yql/guide/usage_info_limits.html

One way around this is obtaining an API key and using it in your app.

https://developer.apps.yahoo.com/dashboard/createKey.html

Best regards,

messages.subject: Re: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
messages.subject_clean: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
messages.body_plain:
It's true that modifying a data.table won't trigger reactivity. We don't have any way to know the data table object has changed.

Also, modifying a reactive values object is an example of a side effect and therefore should be done in an observer, not a reactive expression. If you don't know what I'm talking about, the "Effective reactive programming" videos on https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ go into side effects and observers/reactives in some detail.

Yes I watched the video carefully before, very helpful!

For this particular case, it was intended to update data, add some columns when user switched to one page in Shiny dashboard. I thought about an observer that watch page switching, but that means every page switching will trigger the calculation, sometimes the underlying data didn't change. I tried reactive expression because I want to use the cache feature of it to save some calculations.

Maybe I could try "memoise" package to cache the function, instead of using reactive expression.

For the data.table object, I tried to first assign NULL to the reactive value that hold the data.table object, then assign the updated data.table object again. This caused an infinite loop in reactive expression, but it worked in observer.

So this solved the data.table update problem. I just need to look at if I can cache the calculation with "memoise".

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Yes, actually my original plan of reactive expression is like that, but I ends up modifying reactive values because of another reactive expression, let me see if I can explain the situation as simple as possible.
There are pages for different features in my app:
   page A: some plots. The data is location and time of animal movements. There could be multiple animals in one data set.
   User can select a subset of animals in dataset, and that subset will be the data source for all the plots and features. If no row in a DT is selected, "current page" of the DT is selected. otherwise selected rows of the DT are selected.
   This selection is done by reactive expression "select_data()".
   Page C need to calculate some additional columns which is only used in page C. It also need to use "select_data()" to obtain the subset.

1. I can just obtain the subset then calculate the columns, very simple. But I want to calculate the columns for all animals once then various subset will not need to calculate again. So I decided to change the whole data instead of the subset.

2. If I modify the whole data, I need to use the "select_data()" reactive to select the subset, which I thought it should work because its data source (whole data) has changed.

After fixing the data.table trigger problem, this worked, but there is another problem. Now if user move to page C then move to page A, the underlying data changed so page A plots refreshes, which could take some time, but the data used for plot didn't change.

This just as you said, not an optimal solution. I should keep the extra column separate from page A.

Another solution is copy the whole data, hold in an reactive, use another "select_data" procedure to select the subset again. I just need to abstract the selection process to function, and create two "select_data" reactive, one is solely used for page C.

I wanted to reuse the "select_data" because it's not very simple, turned out this created more problem.

Now when I look back, method 1 of get subset and calculate may not that bad. It will not cause page A refresh, and it's very simple to implement. There could be some extra calculations but that may be faster than plot refreshes. Maybe I tried to optimize too early?

1. Can you paste the entire error from the R console? There should be a stack trace.
2. You're loading all of the data from hadoop into memory, and then doing the filtering in memory. Are you sure you want to do that? It would seem to be better to vary the query depending on what the user has selected. You can do this with dplyr (I wouldn't do this by cobbling together a dynamic SQL query string, that's an easy way to introduce security vulnerabilities). I don't know how easy it is to use ODBC with dplyr today (it may be possible using RODBCDBI and dplyr::src_sql), but in the coming weeks RStudio will be introducing much improved ODBC/dplyr support.

messages.subject: Re: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
messages.subject_clean: reactive expression didn't update when reactive source changed(item in list)
messages.body_plain:
In my previous reply I was trying to introduce as less things as possible from a complex framework, then I forgot one important point:

Page C is to detect outliers in data and remove some points, so it need to update the whole data set...

At first I tried to create a reactive value of points to be removed, then let page A to update plots based on this reactive expression. Later I found I need to update at least subset data in page C, because there could be multiple iterations of
1. remove some points,
2. make some calculations again
3. try to find if there is still points to remove

Each iteration need to update data so the calculation can be based on updated data. I decided to put all the update code in the observer of "remove points", and that will change the whole data. (I saved the removed points so the changes can be undo)

So this is why I need to change the whole data instead of a subset or a copy. It has been some time since I worked on this page, and today I need to fix a new discovered bug, so I was right in choosing update whole data, but forgot the complete reason of this.

One solution I tried today is update whole data when user switched to page C. Make sure it trigger changes in select_data by assign NULL first to the data.table object. The disadvantage of this is that switching to C then A will cause the plot refresh.

So I moved back to my original approach, which actually did the extra calculations needed by page C in page A. I found pure math calculation is often faster than plot refreshes.

The reason that I want to try different approach today is that I found some data break the extra column calculation in page C, and I wanted to isolate that to page C only, so I asked the original question and tried various methods. Now I just will add some more robust method to make sure it doesn't fail with new data.

messages.body_plain:
OK. For things like "remove some points" (and especially if it needs to happen multiple times) then there will definitely need to be some (reactive) state kept somewhere and updated. However, this does NOT mean that these other processes that augment the data frame with additional columns should also be modifying that state. They can still be modeled as reactive expressions that augment the (now-stateful) data.

For representing the data with user-selected points excluded, you can go one of two ways: either have a data frame/table that you remove rows from and then overwrite (as you are doing today), or, leave the original data frame/table alone, and keep a separate vector of row numbers that should be removed. This latter approach can benefit if the removal of rows doesn't inherently necessitate the recalculation of the extra columns; you only have to do the extra-column calculations once, over the whole data, and remove the rows from the already-enhanced table.

I hope this still is still making sense to you, it's hard to do this without working off of an actual concrete example.

messages.body_plain:
The "isolate extra columns to page C" approach have a lot of advantages since it's a better design with less coupling. Previously I need to update the extra columns in several places when needed, now ideally all other changes only update the whole data, and the extra column will be created when moved to page C naturally.

>

I didn't use the row number method because the table could get updated several times, and row number will not be consistent. I can use some unique id in table instead of row number, then I think just keep the "table with points removed" and "all removed points" is simpler.
>
> I realized the extra column calculation could still only apply to current subset, I just need to update the whole data instead of the subset in the actual points removal. This is cleaner in concept, keep the extra column to page C only, with only disadvantage of new calculation on different subset data every time. I tried memoise package but cannot see difference without measuring, it should help.
>
> The plot in page A should not refresh if no point is removed, since the update to whole data only happen when points are actually removed.
>
> Thanks for the discussion!
>
> On Wednesday, May 10, 2017 at 6:38:28 PM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> > OK. For things like "remove some points" (and especially if it needs to happen multiple times) then there will definitely need to be some (reactive) state kept somewhere and updated. However, this does NOT mean that these other processes that augment the data frame with additional columns should also be modifying that state. They can still be modeled as reactive expressions that augment the (now-stateful) data.
> >
> > For representing the data with user-selected points excluded, you can go one of two ways: either have a data frame/table that you remove rows from and then overwrite (as you are doing today), or, leave the original data frame/table alone, and keep a separate vector of row numbers that should be removed. messages.subject: Re: Loading animations for Shiny outputs (shinycssloaders)
messages.subject_clean: Loading animations for Shiny outputs (shinycssloaders)
messages.body_plain:
@Sebastian: Apologies for the late reply, I had some travels and couldn't respond earlier. It's great question, what is happening is that you are using an output (I am guessing some sort of table or data-table) that doesn't have a fixed height. In this case the spinner doesn't know where to center itself vertically, since the server might send back something large or small, it's impossible to know ex-ante.

I have now added on github a quasi-solution that inserts a 'proxy' container in this case which you can configure to be of the height you'd like (the spinner will be centered with respect to the proxy container). The best way to go is to configure the height of the proxy to match what you would expect your output size to be in most cases (except if your outputs are really large in which case a smaller proxy is better, otherwise you won't see the spinner without scrolling). You can test it by installing the latest version from https://github.com/andrewsali/shinycssloaders and playing around with the 'proxy.height' option.

To see how this works in practice, check out: https://frontside.shinyapps.io/table/ - here I use the default height of 400px for the proxy container.

@Joe: Thanks for the report on Type 3, it should be fixed now on the github version, you can verify if the fix is working for you at: https://frontside.shinyapps.io/example/

Cheers,

Andras

messages.body_plain:
I wanted to know is there any graph for plotting the SVM. Or if there is any other method of Visualising SVM for the given dataset

library(e1071)
cmc<-read.table("cmc.data",sep=",")
colnames(cmc) <- c("wifeAge.V1", "wifeEdu.V2","husbandEdu.V3","numChildren.V4","wifeRelig.V5","wifeWorkin.V6","husbandWork.V7","SOLI.V8","MediaExp.V9","contaMethod.V10")

cmc$contaMethod.V10=as.factor(cmc$contaMethod.V10)
intrain <- createDataPartition(y = cmc$contaMethod.V10, p= 0.7, list = FALSE)
trainset<- cmc[intrain,]

testset<- cmc[-intrain,]

model <- svm(contaMethod.V10~., data = trainset)

prediction <- predict(model, testset[,-10])
tab <- table(pred = prediction, true = testset[,10])
confusionMatrix(prediction,testset[,10])

messages.subject: Display first 'n' rows with renderTable()
messages.subject_clean: Display first 'n' rows with renderTable()
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I was wondering if it is possible to display only first few rows when I render a Table/data.frame in UI.

For example, consider below code culled from 'https://gist.github.com/cmishra/87bad81d4eed495272ae'. I would like to display only first 10 rows, and remaining can be hidden from direct view (I can think of adding some vertical scroll bar). There is a similar option available with data.table, however I prefer only to do the same with Table.

Appreciate if someone throw some light on that.

Additionally, I am also wondering how can I add some 'download' button, so that user can download that table/df and save as CSV in disk.

Thanks for your time.

library(shiny)
serverShouldWork <- function(input, output) {
output$bTable <- renderTable({iris}, caption=paste("test"),
caption.placement = getOption("xtable.caption.placement", "top"),
caption.width = getOption("xtable.caption.width", NULL)
)
}
serverDoesWork <- function(input, output) {
output$bTable <- renderTable({iris}, caption="test")
}
ui <- fluidPage("RenderTable Example",
tableOutput("bTable") #table of information on beds (beds)
)
app1 <- shinyApp(ui, serverDoesWork)
app2 <- shinyApp(ui, serverShouldWork)
#runApp(app1)
runApp(app2)

On Thu, May 11, 2017 at 9:07 PM Andras Sali <sali....@gmail.com> wrote:

> @Sebastian: Apologies for the late reply, I had some travels and couldn't respond earlier. It's great question, what is happening is that you are using an output (I am guessing some sort of table or data-table) that doesn't have a fixed height. In this case the spinner doesn't know where to center itself vertically, since the server might send back something large or small, it's impossible to know ex-ante.
>
> I have now added on github a quasi-solution that inserts a 'proxy' container in this case which you can configure to be of the height you'd like (the spinner will be centered with respect to the proxy container). The best way to go is to configure the height of the proxy to match what you would expect your output size to be in most cases (except if your outputs are really large in which case a smaller proxy is better, otherwise you won't see the spinner without scrolling). You can test it by installing the latest version from https://github.com/andrewsali/shinycssloaders and playing around with the 'proxy.height' option.
>
> To see how this works in practice, check out: https://frontside.shinyapps.io/table/ - here I use the default height of 400px for the proxy container.
>

messages.subject: Re: renderValueBox not showing inside tabItem in Shiny
messages.subject_clean: renderValueBox not showing inside tabItem in Shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hi Omar,

in the documentation of tabitem (?tabItem), you can find that you should define a menuitem or menusubitem with the same name.

Below code works for me, can you try it?

library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(

  dashboardHeader(title = "Dynamic boxes"),

  dashboardSidebar(sidebarMenu(menuItem("TotalTVs", tabName = "TotalTVs", icon = icon("dashboard")))),

  dashboardBody(
    tabItems(tabItem(tabName="TotalTVs", valueBoxOutput("vbox")
    )
  )
  )
)

server <- function(input, output) {

  output$vbox <- renderValueBox({
    valueBox(
      "Title",
      200,
      icon = icon("credit-card")
    )
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

best,
Ger

messages.subject: Re: Simulate actionbutton action
messages.subject_clean: Simulate actionbutton action
messages.body_plain:
Can you elaborate on why you actually need to simulate an actionButton click? We explicitly never allow you to change the value of an actionButton because we don't think there's a legitimate use case for this and it promotes bad coding practices in Shiny. See this discussion <https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/167> for an idea of previous discussions and Joe's opinion. This is also why you can change a label of an actionButton (using updateActionButton()), but not its value.

So, in your use case, why not just trigger the same action based on those two different events (event A: when the actionButton input$A is clicked; and event B: when value$val > 100)?

[Aside: as of the release of Shiny 1.0.1 <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/upgrade-1.0.1.html>, we now have a new function called reactiveVal() that allows to create a singe reactive value, instead of requiring you to create a list of reactive values with reactiveValues().]

Here a minimal example, following your scenario:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(
  actionButton("A", "A"),
  numericInput("val", "Val", 10)
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  # this doesn't actually need to be reactive in this example
  RF <- function() {
    print("Either input$val > 100 OR input$A was clicked")
  }

  observeEvent(input$A, { RF() }, ignoreNULL = TRUE)
  observeEvent(req(input$val > 100), { RF() })
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

Use updateNavbarPage().

Minimal example:

library(shiny)

ui <- navbarPage(title = "updateNavbarPage", id = "tabs",
  tabPanel(title = "First Panel", value = "panel1",
    strong("Panel 1"),
    hr(),
    actionButton("go1to2", "Go to 2"),
    actionButton("go1to3", "Go to 3")
  ),
  tabPanel(title = "Second Panel", value = "panel2",
    strong("Panel 2"),
    hr(),
    actionButton("go2to1", "Go to 1"),
    actionButton("go2to3", "Go to 3")
  ),
  tabPanel(title = "Third Panel", value = "panel3",
    strong("Panel 3"),
    hr(),
    actionButton("go3to1", "Go to 1"),
    actionButton("go3to2", "Go to 2")
  )
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {

  observeEvent(c(input$go2to1, input$go3to1), {
    updateNavbarPage(session, "tabs", selected = "panel1")
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  observeEvent(c(input$go1to2, input$go3to2), {
    updateNavbarPage(session, "tabs", selected = "panel2")
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)

  observeEvent(c(input$go1to3, input$go2to3), {
    updateNavbarPage(session, "tabs", selected = "panel3")
  }, ignoreInit = TRUE)
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

messages.body_plain:
RStudio Server Pro is for developing Shiny applications, not deploying them. Shiny Server Pro is used for deploying. There is no max file or memory limit imposed by Shiny itself, but there are obviously going to be inherent limits due to the machine and operating system that you should test yourself first.

Hope that helps!

messages.subject: Re: Module doesn't react to input changes
messages.subject_clean: Module doesn't react to input changes
messages.body_plain:
When passing a reactive expression to a module, you have to ask yourself: Do I want to pass the current value of the reactive expression (i.e. a snapshot in time) to the module, or do I want the module to have access to the current and future values of the reactive? It's almost always the latter. And in that case, in the callModule call you'll omit the parenthesis, and add them inside the module.

So this line:
callModule(downData, 'downCSVdata', 'mydata.csv', dataGen())

becomes this:
callModule(downData, 'downCSVdata', 'mydata.csv', dataGen)

And this line:
write.csv(x = in.data, file = file, row.names = TRUE)

becomes this:
write.csv(x = in.data(), file = file, row.names = TRUE)

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I'm observing this behavior locally - I ran the example "01_hello" from lesson 1 in the RStudio tutorial (http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson1/) and now even if I explicitly invoke another app,
it loads the "01_hello"  app.  When I modified the files, it opened the original files; when I eliminated the files and the directory, it *still* opens them, somehow.

I've restarted RStudio several times, and the behavior persists.

Does anybody know a method of getting it to behave better?

Sincerely,

Barry

On Saturday, July 16, 2016 at 12:41:08 AM UTC-4, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> The problem basically is that Shiny sets its working directory (setwd) once on process startup, and you can think of it being "in" that directory from then on. If you move the directory, it doesn't matter to the R process that Shiny is running in--it moves with it. Only restarting the R process (which by default happens 5 seconds after the last user of that particular app disconnects), which you finally did when you restarted shiny-server, makes the app pick up the new directory at the original path.
>
> I was having trouble imagining how to work around this, but you say that getwd() returns the new path after the directory is moved? This may be a helpful clue... we can try to call setwd if we notice an unexpected change in getwd.
> On Fri, Jul 15, 2016 at 6:04 PM Mike Mehan <mme...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I just got done wrestling with some very strange shiny server behavior and I was wondering if anyone could explain it to me. Here's what happened:
> >
> >
> > I developed a shiny app locally. I had some data that was loaded from a data directory and some stuff in globals.R shared by the ui.R and server.R. I initially deployed my app to my local install of shiny server. Then I made some changes and decided that I should have deployed using svn rather than just copying over the files. I moved the existing folder containing my shiny app to a new folder called archive and then replaced the directory I had just created by checking out the new version from my svn repo. This is when I noticed things started to go wrong, but I had no idea what was causing it. Suddenly variables that I had created in my global.R file weren't being recognized on the server. The app worked perfectly fine on my local machine, then I would deploy via svn and it was like it wasn't reading my global.R properly. So I rewrote the app using renderUI instead of using globals and then I noticed it wasn't registering any changes to my data directory, which was populating the dashboard. It seemed like everything was out of sync. After a lot of debugging I finally printed the working directory of my server-side R session and I noticed that it was set to the archive folder I had made when cleared the way for the svn deploy. Then I tried moving this archive folder into my home directory and sure enough, the shiny app switched over to ~/archive. It was loading server.R and ui.R from the proper place /srv/shiny-server/appName, but the R working directory was following around the shiny app that was originally at that location. I can't wrap my head around how that would happen and was hoping someone smarter could break it down for me.
> >
> > I realize that ran sort of long so here's a shorter list of steps:
> > Deployed app on shiny server by copying ui.R, server.R, global.R, and data_dir to /srv/shiny-server/appName
> > Renamed /srv/shiny-server/appName to /srv/shiny-server/archive
> > Redeployed app on shiny server using svn, to original location: /srv/shiny-server/appName
> > Noticed changes to global.R and contents of data_dir weren't being recognized. All changes to server.R and ui.R were recognized though
> > Printed out R working directory using shinyjs and noticed it was /srv/shiny-server/archive, the original deployment directory
> > Moved the original deploy again, and the working directory followed it
> > Restarted shiny server and problem went away
> >
> > The whole time I was pointing to the same URL. Glad that I finally got it figured out, because it was driving me crazy all day. I did get to learn how to use renderUI so something good came out of it. If anyone can provide any insight that would be great.
> >

  tagList(
    fileInput(ns("file"), label))
}
# Module server function

  colnames<-c("Scan","Tiempo","Global","Difusa","Directa1","Directa2",

  alphacli<-numericInput("alphacli",label=h5(strong("Alpha Cliente")),
                         value=0.0000,step=0.00001,width='80%')
  clit<-numericInput("clit",label=h5(strong("Temperatura de la celula del cliente")),
                     value=25,step=0.25,width='80%')

  # The selected file, if any
  userFile <- reactive({
    # If no file is selected, don't do anything
    input$file
  })

  # The user's data, parsed into a data frame
  datafile <- reactive({
    read.csv(userFile()$datapath,
             sep=",",
             skip=50,
             col.names=colnames,
             fileEncoding="UCS-2LE")
  })

  # Return the reactive that yields the data frame
  return(datafile)
}

messages.subject_clean: Announcement: Shinydashboard 0.6.0 is now on CRAN
messages.body_plain:
Shinydashboard 0.6.0 is now on CRAN! This release of shinydashboard was aimed at both fixing bugs and also bringing the package up to speed with users’ requests and Shiny itself (especially fully bringing bookmarkable state <https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/bookmarking-state.html> to shinydashboard’s sidebar). In addition to bug fixes and new features, we also added a new “Behavior” section <https://rstudio.github.io/shinydashboard/behavior.html> to the shinydashboard website <https://rstudio.github.io/shinydashboard/> to explain this release’s two biggest new features, and also to provide users with more material about shinydashboard-specific behavior.
Sidebar

This release introduces two new sidebar inputs. One of these inputs reports whether the sidebar is collapsed or expanded, and the other input reports which (if any) menu item in the side bar is expanded. In the screenshot below, the Charts tab is expanded.

 <https://rstudioblog.files.wordpress.com/2017/05/sidebar-expanded.png>

These inputs are unusual since they’re automatically available without you needing to declare them, and they have a fixed name. The first input is accessible via input$sidebarCollapsed and can have only two values: TRUE, which indicates that the sidebar is collapsed, and FALSE, which indicates that it is expanded (default).

The second input is accessible via input$sidebarItemExpanded. If no menuItem() in the sidebar is currently expanded, the value of this input is NULL. Otherwise, input$sidebarItemExpanded holds the value of the expandedName of whichever menuItem() is currently expanded (expandedNameis a new argument to menuItem(); if none is provided, shinydashboard creates a sensible default).
Full changes

As usual, you can view the full changelog for shinydashboard in the NEWS <https://github.com/rstudio/shinydashboard/blob/v0.6.0/NEWS.md> file.

messages.body_plain:
The "ERROR: [on_request_read] connection reset by peer" is just a notification that a client (browser) closed a network connection without saying goodbye--you can safely ignore it.

Under no circumstances should "library(shiny)" launch any app--you literally typed that into the console, pressed Enter, and an app launched?

messages.body_plain:
Those input widgets (conf, alphacen, alphacli, clit) should not be defined in the module server function. They should be part of a module UI function (the csvFileInput one? a new plotting-related one? I'm not sure what your intentions are here).

It sounds like your question is how to pass the reactive data that is generated by the csvFile module, to another module that does plotting. You can do that by having your plot module's server function take an additional argument, e.g. `datafile`, and then when invoking that module using callModule, pass the reactive that's returned from csvFile.

i.e. in your app's top-level server function:

datafile <- callModule(csvFile, "datafile")
callModule(plotModule, "plot", datafile)

Note that you pass it without parentheses--you're passing the actual reactive expression object, not just the current value of the reactive expression object. Then in your plotModule code, you can use datafile() inside of reactive expressions or outputs to get the data.

# Module UI function
csvFileInput <- function(id, label = "CSV file") {

  ns <- NS(id)

  tagList(
    fileInput(ns("file"), label))
}
# Module server function

    read.csv(userFile()$datapath,
             sep=",",
             skip=50,
             col.names=colnames,
             fileEncoding="UCS-2LE")
  })

  # Return the reactive that yields the data frame
  return(datafile)
}

plotModule<-function(input,output,session,datafile){

    g1
  })

  return(grafica1)
}

messages.subject: Re: Session object questions
messages.subject_clean: Session object questions
messages.body_plain:
Generally the session object should not be used to store per-user things (with one exception I'll mention in a sec). Rather, declare variables inside the server function; since the server function is run once per session, each session will have its own copy. See more info here: https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

The exception is for package authors who want to offer functions that need to track their own session-specific but internal state. For example I believe shinyjs may use this to ensure it's been initialized before it sends commands to the client. In these cases you don't store things directly on the session object (which you should think of being more like a reference class or R6 object) but in a special environment called session$userData.

messages.subject: Reg : Shiny ::Displaying required field validator message to users
messages.subject_clean: Reg : Shiny ::Displaying required field validator message to users
messages.body_plain:
Hi ,

  I would like to display some required field validator message (Like please enter search keyword) to users whenever they didn’t passed any inputs to textbox and clicked on searched button.

 Here is my sample reproducible code ,please check and advise me .Thanks in Advance ..

​code :

​library(shiny)
library(DT)

ui <- fluidPage(

  headerPanel("test"),
  sidebarLayout(
    sidebarPanel(
      fluidRow(column(6,textInput("NSearch", label = h3("Contacts Search :"))),column (3,actionButton(inputId = "SAction", label = "Search",color= "blue")))
    )
    ,mainPanel(dataTableOutput("d1"))
  )
)

server <- function (input,output){

  observeEvent(input$SAction, {

    validate(
      need(input$NSearch != "" ,  message ="must be provided")

    )

    a = input$NSearch
    b = subset(iris,iris$Sepal.Length > a)
    output$d1 = renderDataTable(b)

  })

}

shinyApp(ui,server)

Manu.

#install_github('radhikesh/d3WordCloudWidget')

library(shiny)
library(d3Histogram)
library(d3WordCloudWidget)

ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(

fluidRow(
column(width = 6, d3HistogramOutput("d3Hist"))),
fluidRow(
column(2, d3WordCloudWidgetOutput(
  "d3Cloud", width = "80%", height = 600
)))
))

server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$d3Hist <- renderD3Histogram({

dataset <- data.frame(lpu = c('Apple','Banana','Orange'), amount =
c(20,10,15))
d3Histogram(dataset = dataset)

})

output$d3Cloud <- renderd3WordCloudWidget({

dm1 <-data.frame(Var1 = c('Apple','Banana','Orange'), Freq = c(20,10,15))
dm1$Var1 <- as.character(dm1$Var1)
d3WordCloudWidget(dm1$Var1, dm1$Freq)

})
})

# Run the application
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

When testing my reproducible example, please comment any one of the output in the ui section d3HistogramOutput or d3WordCloudWidgetOutput and you can see that only one of the widget works at a same time.

Any help would be very much appreciated!

Thanks!

Radhikesh

    ui = graph_shinyUI(paste0("exhibit", btn), paste("Exhibit no.", btn))

and
    callModule(graph_shiny, session$ns(paste0("exhibit", btn)), data_use = data_source)

This part of your d3WordCloudWidget.yaml is wrong:

- name: d3
  version: 3.5.3
  src: htmlwidgets/lib/d3
  script:
          - d3.js
          - d3.layout.cloud.js

Here you're saying that d3.layout.cloud.js is part of d3. But your other widget provides d3 without this JS file. In htmltools/htmlwidgets, if two dependencies have the same name and same version, they are assumed to be substitutes, and one of them is chosen while the other is discarded.

To solve this, in your .yaml file, make a second dependency named "d3cloud" or whatever and move d3.layout.cloud.js (and nothing else) into it. Make sure that the d3 dependency is listed before d3cloud.

>
>
> #library(devtools)

> #install_github('radhikesh/d3WordCloudWidget')
>
> library(shiny)
> library(d3Histogram)
> library(d3WordCloudWidget)
>
>
> ui <- shinyUI(fluidPage(
>
> fluidRow(

> fluidRow(
> column(2, d3WordCloudWidgetOutput(
>   "d3Cloud", width = "80%", height = 600
> )))
> ))
>
>
> server <- shinyServer(function(input, output) {
>
> output$d3Hist <- renderD3Histogram({
>
> dataset <- data.frame(lpu = c('Apple','Banana','Orange'), amount =
> c(20,10,15))
> d3Histogram(dataset = dataset)
>

messages.body_plain:
Any requirements? What kind of plots do you want to make?
Did you have a look at the htmlwidgets page? http://www.htmlwidgets.org/showcase_plotly.html

In my opinion
- D3 makes it possible to make complicated and non-standard plots. You should know javascript (unless you can do with the D3 htmlwidgets that are available)
- Plotly and highcharts are more for standard plots like bar, scatter, pie, etc. If you work a lot with ggplot then choose plotly

The domain argument needs to be a vector of numbers, whereas I think input$population is just a name.

messages.body_plain:
There are several problems:
Minor nit: userFile reactive is just "input$file", I would change this to "req(input$file)"(see https://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/req.html for explanation)
In plotModule function
you are both taking in a datafile argument, and then also calling the csvFile module and assigning the result to datafile. I suspect you just forgot to remove the latter?
In the grafica1 reactive, you need to use `datafile()` instead of `datafile` to access the data.
That said, you should never plot inside of a reactive expression like you are in grafica1. The reason is that reactives cannot be relied on for side effects. I go into this in my Effective Reactive Programming tutorials here: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ Instead, you should give the plotModule a plotModuleUI, and put the plotOutput in there; then instead of a grafica1 reactive you can directly do `output$plot <- renderPlot({ plot(x=datafile()$Tiempo, ...`
After making these fixes I still did not see any data in the data frame--I suspect something's wrong with the CSV reading logic but I couldn't make sense out of your data file.
